general_information.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_information.Description: Description: This course addresses the basic concept of business law in the business environment. The course highlights the basic legal and regulatory requirements by which people and companies conduct business activities. It appreciates the complexities, ambiguities, and many areas of the law in undertaking business. Furthermore, it will focus on business ethics, which emphasizes the appropriate behaviors and treatments of business entities in global and local contexts. Objectives: Upon completing this course, student can demonstrate knowledge about the legal system and basic principles of business law as well as the relationship between ethics and regulations in the business environment. Students can compare the legal requirements and legal provisions of managing companies in the US and Vietnam and then ethically evaluate the application of laws in business transactions. Students are expected to be able to identify essential solutions for business disputes in compliance with applicable laws.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by the instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purposes - Read the textbook in advance - Keep in touch with the lecturer regularly for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online support from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.
general_information.Tools: - Textbook and all learning materials provided on FLM: flm.fpt.edu.vn/ - Internet

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: LO1. Describe the legal system, legal environment and basic principles of business law
LO2. Define the relationships of ethics and law in business
LO3. Describe the current law and regulations in corporation
LO4. Describe the current law and regulations applied to business transactions
LO5. Apply ethic consideration in business context
LO6. Apply current law, rules, and regulations related to settling business disputes
Have a sense of discipline, professional manners and a high respect of the law

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: OP1: Guideline: on session 1 Moot court: are held respectively on session: 28,29,30,31 (moot court 1); 40,41,42,43 (moot court 2); 54,55,56,57 (moot court 3). 1. Cases for Moot court: U.S case, assigned by Lecturer. 2. Preparation: Costume and Equipments are taken at Administrative Department and preserved by Students till the last moot court. 3. Groups: 06. Two groups will represent for DEFENDANT and PLAINTIFF respectively to work together on 01 moot court with 01 case. Each group comprises of 4 students at least. 4. Language: English mainly. 5. Participants in 01 moot court: all lawyers in 2 moot court-groups, 01 chairman of JURIES and 03 JUDGES (elected by Lecturer in non-moot court groups). 6. Steps to hold a moot court: 6.1. Arrangement of court room, get ready on gowns. 6.2. Plaintiff and Defendant present FACT of the case (play, video, ppt) 6.3. Juries and Judges make questions regarding the FACT. 6.4. Plaintiff and defendant making a debate regarding ISSUES of the case. Judges can make questions to clear down the argument. 6.5. After debate, Juries make questions regarding all the ISSUES. 6.6. Decision of Judges and Juries: Juries votes for the winner with ballot. Judges decides the stronger group. Judges and Chairman of Juries give the comment for weakness and strength of both sides. 6.7. Results: decided by Voting of Juries and Decision of Judges. If they are opposite to each other. The Lecturer will decide. Further guidance, please refer to INDIVIDUAL AND ASSIGNMENT GUIDELINE attached to Course Implementation Plan Submit report: as requested by the lecturer for every moot court OP2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal
